sections.name: Radscorpions
sections.card:
Summary: Big armored scorpions of the Mojave that run straight at you in packs of two to five, striking with claws and a poisoned tail. They are rough on a low-level Courier, and Damage Threshold means an unprepared Courier struggles to put them down.
Weak points: The claws carry lighter armor than the body does, and crippling them stuns the scorpion. Armor-piercing weapons do well against it, with the Guns skill. It has no head or other spot that takes extra damage, so V.A.T.S. and firearms do somewhat worse.
Looks like: A regular scorpion in everything but size, with a blotchy, dark bluish-gray armored shell. The common kind runs from about a big dog's size up to a small farm animal's, and the rare queen is bigger than a Corvega.
Tips: The giant radscorpion is rarer and faster, hits much harder and has a Damage Threshold like a sentry bot's, and some stand just outside Goodsprings and its cemetery, so you can meet one very early. Only two queens are known: one is south of the Nipton Road pit stop, in the scorpion burrow, and the other is in the Searchlight fire station, reached during a side quest. Ruby Nash will cook you a casserole if you bring her a radscorpion gland.

sections.name: Geckos
sections.card:
Summary: Reptile packs found across the whole Mojave. When one gecko fights, the whole pack joins in, charging or leaping in with open jaws and clawing quickly. Some kinds breathe fire or spit poison from a distance.
Looks like: A lizard with two fins behind its head, eyes with an orange tint, and fingers and toes, five of each. Size depends on the kind, from a small child's height to taller than a grown adult. Golden geckos are bright gold; fire geckos are blotchy purple and red with spikes along the back.
Tips: Plain geckos, the mildest kind, roam around Goodsprings and near the Mojave Outpost, and along Interstate 15 toward Primm. Golden geckos live in irradiated places such as Crescent Canyon, Vault 34 and Cottonwood crater, and their attacks do heavy radiation damage. Fire geckos favor mountains and caves such as Lucky Jim Mine and Nopah Cave. The Animal Friend perk works on geckos and golden geckos but not on fire geckos, which run if hit by a flare gun. Tanned gecko hides can be made into armor.

sections.name: Giant mantises
sections.card:
Summary: Mutated praying mantises that came out of Vault 22 and spread across the Mojave. Each is much smaller than a person, so they swarm whenever they can and mostly leap in to slice with their forelegs.
Weak points: Cripple its antennae and a mantis goes into a frenzy, attacking anything near enough to reach.
Looks like: Much like a real praying mantis, only far bigger, though still smaller than a person. The young nymphs are much smaller than the adults. The Zion Canyon kinds are larger.
Tips: Weak nymphs turn up early in the Goodsprings schoolhouse and Nevada Highway Patrol station; the adults wait later, around Spring Mt. Ranch State Park and on the road toward Jacobstown. A shot ootheca lets out a dozen nymphs, which come at you. Some nymphs die just from being stepped on. Dead mantises can yield eggs and forelegs.

sections.name: Super mutants and nightkin
sections.card:
Summary: Tough armored mutants that favor heavy guns, plus melee weapons like the super sledge. Gunners walk slowly toward you while firing; melee fighters throw frag grenades and then rush in. Plain mutants give way to brutes and masters as you level.
Looks like: Brutes can be told apart by helmets and rough metal armor. Nightkin skin is a dark blue tinged with purple, and they wear no armor.
Tips: Ordinary super mutants are armored to Damage Threshold 15, the same as combat armor; nightkin wear none but shrug off 30 percent of damage. Nightkin use Stealth Boys to creep up on their prey. Their main base in the Mojave is Black Mountain. Hostile ones reliably come back at Black Rock Cave, Jack Rabbit Springs and a small cave north of Ranger Station Bravo. Hostile ones often carry miniguns, light machine guns or super sledges that you can sell.

sections.name: Centaurs
sections.card:
Summary: Mutants that are somewhat humanoid in shape. They fire a slow, high-arcing radioactive spit and whip at close range with their tongues. One alone is no great danger, but they rarely come alone.
Weak points: They are slow and clumsy, and the spit travels so slowly that it is easy to sidestep.
Looks like: The common kind has only a head and chest like a person's, with three long tongues like tentacles where back spines would be. Evolved centaurs are larger and more muscled, with dense clumps of tumors on their backs.
Tips: The tongue lash does little physical damage but a notable amount of radiation. Groups gather at Jack Rabbit Springs, south of Black Mountain, and in the Devil's Throat east of Bitter Springs, where evolved ones and the single giant evolved centaur stay. They respawn there three days after being killed.

sections.name: Bighorners
sections.card:
Summary: Mutated sheep, grazing wild in herds of three to seven or kept by settlements like Goodsprings and Jacobstown. They leave you alone until you or their young get close, then they bellow, charge and ram, and the entire herd joins in if one of them is upset.
Weak points: They are about as hardy as a radscorpion. Hits to the horns are treated as head shots, and a critical hit blows the head apart.
Looks like: A horned sheep; every bighorner grows horns, whatever its sex. Bulls are larger and stronger, and the young are about a third of full size.
Tips: The compass shows them hostile, but unprovoked ones do not chase you; leave them be and they graze. Their head-butts are brutal, flinging you back or knocking you down, and they run very fast; bulls in a group keep knocking you over. Hurting one of the young turns its relatives on you, and penned calves in towns are watched by ranchers who turn hostile if you harm them. Take the Animal Friend perk and they never turn on you.

sections.name: Giant ants
sections.card:
Summary: Large insects with big mandibles that can be a real nuisance early in the game. Workers wear you down with nonstop swarming attacks, and soldiers are the biggest of the usual kinds.
Weak points: Striking an ant's antennae counts as a critical hit and sends it into a frenzy. A worker's shell is not especially hard next to a radscorpion's.
Looks like: A big ant in a yellow-brown shell with large mandibles and long antennae. The queen is the biggest creature anywhere in the Mojave.
Tips: They are not fast, so if you fight them from a distance you can simply walk away from them. Workers roam in groups across barren desert, including the Ivanpah race track and Ivanpah Dry Lake; several soldiers are inside the Allied Technologies offices. One queen exists, in the mound south of those offices. At the Nellis array the ants blow up if hit by energy weapons or explosives.

sections.name: Feral ghouls
sections.card:
Summary: Ghouls that lost their minds to heavy radiation exposure and attack everyone except their own kind. Shrill and fast, they are dangerous mainly in numbers or to a low-level Courier.
Weak points: A plain feral ghoul goes down after a headshot or two from a reasonable ranged weapon, or one good melee hit, armed or unarmed.
Looks like: Like normal ghouls but with deformed faces, skinnier, and moving oddly. The plain kind wears only tattered shorts; reavers have scraps of metal armor on them.
Tips: A roamer is a bigger threat than the plain kind, and far more common, though a reaver is stronger still. At low levels a reaver is only a bit stronger than a roamer, and in the Mojave it no longer gives off radiation. Glowing ones turn up at higher levels where radiation is worst, with much more health and damage and a burst of radiation. Expect ferals in the Vegas sewers and around Hell's Motel, the Devil's Throat and the Nevada Highway Patrol station. The armor they wear is for show.

sections.name: Sentry bots
sections.card:
Summary: Heavy military robots on wheeled tripod legs, armed with a Gatling laser or minigun on one arm and, on the other arm, a missile launcher. They have a lot of health, so they are hard to put down, especially at a low level.
Weak points: It is a robot, so electromagnetic pulses hit it hard: pulse mines, pulse grenades and other EMP weapons can all damage it badly. Destroying the combat inhibitor on its back makes it go berserk and lash out at everything near it.
Looks like: Armored head, wheeled tripod base. The REPCONN ones are shorter, with green eyes instead of red and REPCONN in white across the chest.
Tips: At long range a sentry bot leans on its missiles; once you are close it switches to the minigun or Gatling laser to avoid splash on itself. Head shots do less damage to it. Hardened sentry bots, met with hardened Mister Gutsies near the crashed vertibird, have about 500 hit points against 300 but no armor at all, and resist pulse grenades better. Twelve REPCONN bots hide in the headquarters and come out if you trip the alarm.

sections.name: Fiends
sections.card:
Summary: A gang of raiders who are all chem users driven mad, working the outskirts of New Vegas and holding the southwestern ruins of Vegas. They fight in small war parties.
Looks like: Red eyes, always, from constant chem use. They wear assorted raider armor, and each helmet is distinctive, decorated with the skull of a ruminant painted for war.
Tips: Their melee gear includes knives and pool cues, and for guns they mostly carry silenced .22 SMGs, varmint rifles and caravan shotguns, plus an unusual number of Laser RCWs and plasma rifles. Close to a dozen spots spawn Fiends from 0600 to 2230, and none spawn from 2230 to 0600, so night is the calmer time to cross the Vegas countryside. Everyone but the Great Khans is a target. With a Speech of 65 you can pass as a Great Khan chem seller to the guard of Vault 3, which makes the Fiends inside peaceful; those outside stay hostile.

sections.name: Stimpaks
sections.card:
Summary: A medicine you inject to heal yourself, restoring hit points and limb condition.
Uses: Base healing is 30 hit points and limb condition, and it grows with your Medicine skill, from 36 hit points at skill 10 to 90 at skill 100. In Hardcore mode it heals over time instead and cannot mend a crippled limb; for that you need a doctor or an item that says it heals limbs, such as Hydra or a doctor's bag.
Tips: You can craft one at a workbench from a broc flower, an empty syringe and a xander root with Science 70. Most doctors sell them, and Cliff Briscoe in Novac nearly always has some. With a good reputation among the Followers of the Apocalypse, Julie Farkas at the Old Mormon Fort hands out one free each day. Doc Mitchell's house holds three.

sections.name: Doctor's bags
sections.card:
Summary: A consumable that mends crippled limbs and keeps working in Hardcore mode, where stimpaks cannot.
Uses: Used plainly, it gives every limb a small boost; applied from the stats screen to one limb, it fixes far more. In Hardcore mode a doctor, Hydra, sleeping in a bed you own, or the Honest Hearts items healing poultice, daturana and weapon binding ritual will also mend crippled limbs.
Tips: You can craft one at a workbench with Medicine 40 from forceps, a medical brace, a scalpel and surgical tubing. Early ones sit in the Goodsprings gas station and in Doc Mitchell's house, and Doc Mitchell gives two more during Ghost Town Gunfight if your Medicine is 30. Viper gunslingers rarely carry one.

sections.name: RadAway and Rad-X
sections.card:
Summary: Two radiation chems that work at opposite ends: Rad-X raises your resistance before you go into a hot zone, and RadAway clears radiation after exposure. Neither is addictive.
Uses: RadAway always removes 50 rads plus your Medicine skill, from 60 at skill 10 to 150 at skill 100; in Hardcore mode it works over ten seconds. Rad-X gives resistance for four minutes, from 30 percent at skill 10 to 75 percent at skill 100. More doses lengthen the time but do not stack the strength, and resistance tops out at 85 percent, so no gear makes you immune.
Tips: Doctors often stock RadAway: Doc Mitchell (Goodsprings), Dr. Ada Straus (Novac) and Senior Scribe Linda Schuler (Hidden Valley bunker). Most shops hold at most three RadAway, and some hold none. Vault 34's clinic safe holds both chems, and Charleston Cave has three Rad-X. Twenty doses of RadAway earns the Free Radical perk.

sections.name: Stealth Boys
sections.card:
Summary: A stealth gadget with a disc worn on the wrist or an emitter carried in a belt pouch, which makes the wearer hard to see for a short while. In the Mojave, nightkin are the ones you usually see carrying them.
Uses: One gives +100 Sneak and +75 Stealth Field for two real minutes, which is one in-game hour. A second one used while the first runs adds another in-game hour to what is left. The Chemist perk, the Day Tripper perk and the Logan's Loophole trait stretch the time. The Sneak boost also helps stealth-based Speech checks, and pulse grenades do not affect the device.
Tips: Early ones: a locked safe in the Goodsprings schoolhouse (Lockpick 25), and one beside a skeleton at Jack Rabbit Springs. The REPCONN test site holds six in fixed spots, and nightkin bodies there may give more. Vikki and Vance Casino pays one out as a prize once you have won 1,250 chips or more.
